recipes.name: Ronaldo's Beef Carnitas
ingredients_raw: 1 (4 ounce) can green chile peppers, chopped

steps.text: Preheat oven to 300 degrees F (150 degrees C).
Place roast on heavy foil large enough to enclose the meat. In a small bowl, combine the green chile peppers, chili powder, oregano, cumin, garlic and salt to taste. Mix well and rub over the meat.
Totally wrap the meat in the foil and place in a roasting pan.
Bake at 300 degrees F (150 degrees C) for 3 1/2 to 4 hours, or until the roast just falls apart with a fork. Remove from oven and shred using two forks.

raw_recipe.headline: Ronaldo's Beef Carnitas
raw_recipe.description: Chuck roast is wrapped in foil with Mexican-style seasonings, and cooked at low temperature until it is tender and shreds easily. This is served in flour tortillas. Leftovers freeze well.

review.reviewBody: I made this in the crockpot and it turned out fabulous! I doubled the chile peppers and seasonings, wrapped the whole works in foil and cooked it in the crockpot for 8 hours on low. After the 8 hours was up I removed the foil package, dumped all the liquid into a bowl and skimmed the fat off the top and then shredded the meat and put it back into the crockpot with a small amount of the defatted liquid and cooked it for an additional 30 minutes or so. I served the shredded meat on warm flour tortillas with shredded monterey jack and cheddar cheese, sour cream and salsa. I made some Zatarain's Spanish Rice to serve on the side - it goes really good with this, especially if you add a can of diced tomatoes w/ peppers to the rice while it is cooking - and you could also put a little bit of the rice in the tortilla along with the meat if you wanted to - that's how my hubbie ate his! This was REALLY GOOD and I'll definitely be making it again!

Since I used 2 separate chuck roasts, I doubled the rub recipe and added 4 tsp salt. I wrapped it in a foil packet and put it in my Instapot with a bit of water in the bottom (2-3 cups), with the peat titling on a rack that came with the Instapot. I put it on the meat/stew setting for 3 hours, and it was fall apart tender.

Sooooo good! I only had one pound of beef stew meat so that’s what I used. I mixed all of the spices in a bowl with some water added to it and I poured it over the meat and mixed it with a spoon. I wrapped it up in foil and I put that foil packet into the crockpot. I cooked it on low for 8 hours. It was delicious! If I were to use a 4 pound roast I would probably triple the spices in the recipe

I did not make exactly as directed, but regardless it's a 5 star. I used a 2 pound roast instead of a 4, but kept the other measurements the same. I also added a few jalapeno slices for just a little more kick. Lastly, instead of wrapping and baking, I used the slow cook function of my pressure cooker. I cooked it for 4 hours on high. At about 3 hours, I removed the meat and cut it into smaller pieces to help speed up the break-down. Fantastic recipe and I will make again.

I had to improvise with this one. I halved the recipe using a 2 lb. chuck roast that I cut into large chunks. I didn’t use the green chile peppers, but instead used a can of Rotel tomatoes. I browned the meat on the stovetop first and then added it to my crockpot. I skipped the foil altogether. Then I deglazed the pan with the tomatoes, scraping up all the yummy browned bits and added that to the crockpot. I cooked this on low for 7 hours, at which point it was moist and shredded perfectly. I served this in warmed tortillas with, green onions, chopped tomatoes, salsa and sour cream, along with Mexican Rice III, also from this site. We really enjoyed this dinner. I put my leftovers in the freezer for a quick and easy meal another night!

I followed the recipe from Cindi M and used the crockpot. Wrapped the 3.26 chuck roast in foil, doubled spices, 1 can of chilis and cooked 8 hrs overnight. It was perfect! Poured juice in bowl and froze it while I shredded it pulling off any fat and gristle. after mall amount of fat solidified, scraped it off, put beef in juices and refrigerated. Before serving my guests, I put in sheet pan and broiled to crisp it. Did not put in tortilla..used as main dish served with basmati wild rice mix, fresh local tomatoes on lettuce, asparagus with lemon juice and a redskin potato salad. It was a hit!

Tender and delicious shredded beef tacos. These were absolutely wonderful. Modified the recipe a little, mostly as recommended by other reviewers: Used tri-tip roast (2lb size was plenty for two people) but kept spices same volume as indicated in this recipe (since others recommended doubling spices for original recipe at 4lbs). Cooked in crock pot on high for 7 hours. Prepared by seasoning roast with spices as a rub, then placed in crock pot in a broth of: green chiles (used half hot and half mild), 2 diced garlic cloves, 4oz jalapeno tomato sauce, one can of beef broth, and 2 chopped jalapeno peppers. Did not wrap in foil but the meat eventually cooked tender in broth. Finally shredded the beef and placed in soft taco shells with guac, sour cream, and fine shredded cheese. SO TENDER and came out just slightly spicy...the best beef tacos we've ever made at home. Thanks for sharing this recipe!

This was quite good. I used a 2.5 lb. roast and doubled the rest of the ingredients and cooked in the slow cooker for 8 hrs. Made "burrito bols" using rice, black beans, cheese, garden fresh salsa and lettuce. Very nice meal. Thank you for sharing your recipe!

I made this only thing I did was a little differently I added a extra tablespoon of all the seasonings and then I had a Hatch pepper and I put all the seasonings in a plastic bag cut up the roast and small pieces left it overnight with the seasonings as a rub dumped everything into the slow cooker and let it cook shredded it and I've used it for everything including Pizza

This recipe was great! I used a smaller roast (a little under 2lbs), but doubled the seasoning anyway and it came out delicious. Per another reviewer's suggestion, I wrapped the seasoned roast in foil, then cooked it in the crock pot on high for 5 hours. Then I removed the meat, transferred the juices back into the crock pot, put the meat back, and shredded it with two forks. I cooked it for an additional 30 mins on low. Perfect for tacos!
Used all the spices but only about 2 lbs of meat. Turned out great. I also seperated the beef at 3-1/2 hours and put it uncovered in oven set to broil to crisp it up for the last 20 minutes.
I did the wrap in foil/crock pot method. Perfect. I am going to add more spice to the rub next time.,
really good and cristiano Ronaldo is the goat

Wrapping the meat in foil is the key, I think, for getting melt in the mouth meat. The spice flavors didn't come through very much until the leftovers sat in the juices in the frig overnight. I was pleasantly surprised by the amount of liquid after cooking. I think next time I will shred the meat, and let it sit in the juices a bit before serving.
Love it! This one I will keep in my pocket for hosting. So easy! I am also planning to try it with breakfast tacos (beef, eggs, cheese, salsa verde). Yum!!
Delicious go-to for fall apart mexican beef! I use it for tacos, burritos and quesadillas!
I've made this several times. Cook slow and low so it doesn't dry out. You can cook this in the smoker and crockpot. When I use the crockpot I add beer or broth with lime juice.
I used a 3 lb chuck roast, doubled the spices. Rushed out really good. Cooked for 4 hours... didn't shed too easily, so I chopped/ shredded it. Tasted great!

This recipe was delicious! I used a rump roast and cooked it in the crockpot with a little beef broth. Turned out perfect! Ate as tacos one night, used the leftovers to make enchiladas for another meal. Our family of four had enough meat for three dinners. Will make again!
Awesome recipe. My kids want this at least once a week. Didn’t change a thing. Went directly by the recipe and love it
